title: Card payments for every element of your node
description: The Stripe element of a Fractera node keeps your Stripe keys, creates payment links on Stripe Checkout and records each payment for the element that sold.
keywords: Stripe, Stripe Checkout, card payments, webhook, Stripe MCP, Claude Code, Fractera, open source

blocks.pill: OpenSource Web4 agent & app starter kit
blocks.title: Card payments for every element of your node
blocks.description: Your shop or booking page asks this element for a payment link with one call. The buyer pays on Stripe's own page, and the money goes to your Stripe account.

blocks.text: Asks for a payment link: the amount, the currency and its own order number.
Creates a Stripe Checkout session with your keys and returns its link.
Takes the card on Stripe's side, so card numbers never pass through your computer.
Receives the money at Stripe's own prices. Fractera adds no fee.
Stripe then sends a signed event back, and the element records it for the element that sold: paid, failed, expired or refunded.

head: Without it
With the Stripe element
rows: Each site needs its own Stripe integration
Each element makes one call and gets a payment link
Your Stripe keys are copied into every project
The keys live in this element and are checked with Stripe before they are saved
Every app writes and protects its own webhook
One webhook checks Stripe's signature and records each event once
You check each app to see whether an order was paid
One question per order returns paid, open or expired
Your coding agent writes payment code from memory
Your agent follows Stripe's own skill and works through Stripe's MCP server

blocks.title: An agent that knows your Stripe account

blocks.text: This element's agent connects to Stripe's MCP server with an agent key. It can read and set up your account: products, prices, webhook endpoints and the history of a payment.

An agent key is a restricted key you create in Stripe for agents. Stripe holds payouts, refunds and account changes made with it until a reviewer approves them, and a refund asked through MCP reaches you as a link to confirm.

items: `use-stripe`: the rules of this element. Which tool fits which job, a sandbox before live keys, refunds wait for a person, keys appear only by name.
`stripe-best-practices`: Stripe's own skill on Checkout, keys and webhooks.

blocks.title: Turn it on in four steps

items: Copy the publishable and secret keys from [dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys](https://dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys). Start with the test keys of a sandbox.
On [dashboard.stripe.com/webhooks](https://dashboard.stripe.com/webhooks), create an event destination for `https://stripe.<your domain>/api/stripe-webhook` and copy its signing secret.
For the agent's Stripe tools, create a restricted key on the API keys page and choose "Authorizing agent access to your account".
In your node, open Stripe, then Settings, Payments, Web2. Paste the keys, save, and turn the element on in its Danger zone.

blocks.text: The secret key and the agent key are checked with Stripe before they are saved. The page shows only which keys are set, never their values.
An element of your node takes a payment with one call to this element, using the node key it already has. It never holds Stripe keys of its own.

On its success page the element asks `stripe-status` whether the order was paid, and `stripe-payments` returns its whole journal. Your element's agent finds this element by its role in the node and takes the call examples from its card.

head: Part
What it does
rows: `stripe-checkout`
Creates a Stripe Checkout session and returns the payment link
`stripe-status`
Returns paid, open or expired for a session
`stripe-payments`
Returns the journal of one element
`stripe-webhook`
Receives Stripe's events, checks the signature and writes one line per event, without buyer data
`stripe-agent`
Stripe's MCP server for this element's agent, opened by the agent key
`use-stripe`, `stripe-best-practices`
The agent's skills: this element's rules and Stripe's own advice
`stripe` 23.0.0
Stripe's Node.js library inside the doors
Tests
35 checks that run without network; webhook events are signed with Stripe's own library
Programs on your computer
None. The element needs no Stripe plugin and no Stripe CLI

blocks.text: Subscriptions, refunds from your own interface, Stripe Connect or a card form of your own: ask this element's agent. It adds a new door with the same library and tests it, following Stripe's skill.

Built by Fractera for the [Lagrix](https://lagrix.dev) protocol and for any web2 project that needs fast development, few tokens and high load. Used with Claude Code. The code is open under the MIT license: [Fractera/fractera-stripe-starter](https://github.com/Fractera/fractera-stripe-starter).
